public_rationale: Under the stated funding-allocation reading, 'AI and very little else' is contradicted. Crunchbase reported that AI received about 11% of global venture funding in July 2023. Investment outside AI was therefore substantial. Contemporary investor interviews do support enthusiasm for AI, so the finding does not reject that narrower observation. The result depends on treating investment allocation as evidence of focus; the sources do not settle a claim solely about excitement or conversation.
limitations: Crunchbase includes seed, angel, venture, corporate-venture and private-equity rounds in venture-backed companies, a broader universe than traditional venture funds alone.
The July data reflect reporting as of August 4 and are subject to reporting lags.
Completed investments can reflect decisions made before July.
The unspecified quality and availability of alternative companies are not separately graded.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of August 2023, venture capital is focused on AI and little else, despite there being plenty of revenue-generating companies with good ideas to invest in.

statement.excerpt: There are plenty of companies to invest in, companies that have good ideas that generate revenues, but venture is still enamored with AI and very little else.

from_speaker: venture is still enamored with AI and very little else
plenty of companies to invest in
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that venture investors overwhelmingly favor AI, with little investment interest extending to other businesses.
Use actual funding allocation as an observable measure of investment interest. Enthusiasm and completed investments can differ.
Use July 2023, the latest complete calendar month before the August 10 post, for the ongoing observation.
Read the unqualified reference to venture capital as industry-wide; use global funding data.
Treat 'good ideas' as an evaluative description. The central testable assertion is the claimed concentration on AI, rather than the investment merits of unspecified companies.
criteria.support_condition: Industry-wide evidence shows investment overwhelmingly concentrated in AI, with other sectors receiving only marginal funding and attention.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Industry-wide evidence shows substantial investment continuing outside AI, with AI accounting for only a minority of funding. This contradicts the concentration assertion under the funding-allocation reading, even if enthusiasm for AI was strong.
